welcome.title: See what’s coming. Know your next step. Never take it alone.
welcome.lead: Waypoint is a free companion for big changes — losing a job, starting out, moving country, or learning something new. It shows you one clear next step at a time.
welcome.checkMessageHint: Paste a text, link or offer. Nothing is stored.
welcome.getHelpHint: Emergency numbers and support lines for your country.
welcome.askHint: An AI guide that knows its limits and puts your safety first.
welcome.point1Body: Not a feed. Today shows the one thing that moves you forward, and how long it takes.
welcome.point2Title: Plans that are honest about time
welcome.point2Body: Week-by-week plans built from real skills and free courses, sized to the hours you actually have.
welcome.point3Body: Private things are encrypted, nothing optional is on by default, and you can export or delete everything at any time.
welcome.freeNote: Free for individuals. Works on low-cost phones and slow connections.

auth.signUpFailed: We couldn’t create the account. Check your details and try again.
auth.checkBody: We’ve sent an email to {email}. Open the link in it to confirm your address, then sign in with your password.
auth.checkExisting: Already have an account with this address? Then the email tells you how to sign in instead.
auth.checkSpam: It can take a few minutes, so check your spam folder too. The link works for 24 hours, and signing in before you confirm sends a new one.
auth.checkGuest: What you did as a guest moves into your account the first time you sign in on this device.
auth.guestPending: You’re using Waypoint as a guest. Sign in to the account you created, and what you did as a guest moves into it.
auth.guestKeep: Bring what I did as a guest into this account

auth.confirmSent: Link sent to {email}. Open it within 24 hours to confirm your address.
auth.confirmedBody: You can now sign in with your email address and password. Opening the link didn’t sign you in.
auth.confirmedBodySignedIn: You can now answer invitations sent to this address.
auth.confirmedGuest: Sign in on this device to bring along what you did as a guest.
auth.confirmFailedLead: It may have expired or already been used.
auth.confirmFailedBody: Links work for 24 hours. Sign in with your email and password, and we’ll send you a new one.

shield.identifiersHint: One per line. We keep only a coded version to spot repeat scammers.

money.title: Money
money.lead: How long your money lasts, what to do first, and how to keep it safe.
money.privacy: Your numbers are encrypted and only you can see them. Waypoint never shares them or uses them for ads.
money.disclaimer: General information, not financial advice. Waypoint doesn’t sell loans, cards or investments.
money.introTitle: Get your bearings in two minutes
money.introBody: Rough numbers are fine. You’ll see how long your savings last at this rate, and the steps that help most right now.
money.incomeMonths: What came in over recent months
money.incomeMonthsHint: Waypoint plans with a lean month, not your best one.
money.incomeMonth: {count, plural, one {Last month} other {# months ago}}
money.essentialsHint: Leave out anything that doesn’t apply.
money.otherHint: Eating out, subscriptions, gifts — the things you could pause.
money.debtHint: Loans, cards, buy-now-pay-later and money owed to people.
money.savingsHint: Money you could reach within a few days if you had to.
money.clearConfirm: Delete your money numbers? Your plan and everything else stays.

stable.label: Steady
stable.title: You’re on steady ground
stable.body: Your income covers your month. A good time to grow a buffer and invest in your next skill.

watch.label: Watch
watch.title: Worth keeping an eye on
watch.body: Things work for now, but there’s little room for surprises.

tight.label: Tight
tight.title: Money is tight
tight.body: More is going out than coming in, or debt takes a big share. A few steps now can buy you time.

critical.label: Urgent
critical.title: This needs attention now
critical.body: At this rate your money runs out soon. Start with the essentials — you don’t have to sort this out alone.

money.runwayMonths: {months, plural, one {About # month at this rate} other {About # months at this rate}}
money.runwayLessThanMonth: Less than a month at this rate
money.runwayNone: Your savings aren’t being used up
money.runwayNoneBody: What comes in covers what goes out, so your savings stay where they are.
money.statDebt: Of income goes to debt payments

protect-essentials.title: Protect the essentials first
protect-essentials.detail: Rent, food, power, medicine and minimum debt payments come before everything else. List them and pay them first each month.

talk-to-lenders.title: Talk to lenders before you miss a payment
talk-to-lenders.detail: Most banks and lenders have hardship options (a pause, lower payments or a longer term), and they are easier to get before a payment is missed.

avoid-high-cost-credit.title: Avoid instant-loan apps and payday loans
avoid-high-cost-credit.detail: They can charge very high fees and some use harassment to collect. If a lender pressures you, stop and check it in Shield.

check-benefits.title: Check the support you are entitled to
check-benefits.detail: Many people miss unemployment, food, housing or health support they qualify for. The Services checklist for your situation lists where to start.

trim-other.title: Pause one non-essential cost this month
trim-other.detail: Pick the easiest one to pause, not the one you feel worst about. Small, reversible cuts are easier to keep.

income-step.title: Add one income step to your plan
income-step.detail: A short-term task, a few hours of paid work or selling something unused can buy time while your longer plan runs.

emergency-buffer.title: Build a small buffer
emergency-buffer.detail: Aim first for one month of essentials, set aside automatically on payday, even in small amounts.

grow-buffer.title: Grow your buffer to three months
grow-buffer.detail: Three months of essentials gives you room to choose your next job rather than take the first one.

reduce-debt.title: Bring debt payments down
reduce-debt.detail: Debt payments above about a third of income leave little room for surprises. Pay the highest-interest debt first, and never borrow to repay.

invest-in-skills.title: Put a little towards your next skill
invest-in-skills.detail: With essentials covered, a small, regular amount for learning or tools tends to pay back faster than most alternatives.

free-advice.title: Get free, independent debt advice
free-advice.detail: Non-profit debt advice services can negotiate with lenders for you. Avoid anyone who charges upfront to “clear” your debt.

money.overwhelmed: Money worries can weigh heavily. If it’s getting too much, talk to someone.
money.safety1: Never pay a fee to get a loan, a job or a prize.
money.safety2: Borrow only from lenders registered with your central bank.
money.safety3: Never share a one-time code, PIN or password — not even with “bank staff”.
money.safety4: Guaranteed high returns are a scam signal.
money.safetyCheck: Check a message or offer in Scam Shield

circles.lead: Small groups of people going through the same change. Share what’s working, ask questions and keep each other going.

circles.nameHint: A first name or nickname works best. Leave it empty to appear as “{member}”.
circles.accept: I’ve read the guidelines and will follow them
circles.joinedNew: That circle had just filled up, so we opened a new one on the same topic for you.
circles.joinLimit: You can be in up to five circles. Leave one to join another.
circles.nameContact: Use a first name or nickname, without phone numbers, emails or ID numbers.
circles.mutedNote: Reminders from this circle are off.
circles.leaveBody: Your posts stay in the circle, shown as from a former member. You can join again later if there’s a place.

bodyLabels.question: What would you like to ask?
bodyLabels.checkin: How are you doing this week?

circles.bodyHint: Please don’t share phone numbers, addresses or bank details. They’re hidden if you do.

held.scamBody: Parts of this looked like a common scam, so a moderator will check it before others can see it.
held.crisisBody: It sounded like things may be really hard right now, so we kept this post private. You don’t have to handle this alone.
held.reportedBody: Some members reported this post. A moderator will look at it soon.

circles.feedEmpty: No posts yet. Why not say hello and share what you’re working on?
circles.reportLead: Reports are anonymous. Nobody is told who reported.
circles.worriedHint: We’ll send them a gentle note with support options. We won’t say who asked or which post.
circles.scamHint: Don’t reply to, pay or share details with anyone who contacts you about it.
circles.reportedToast: Thank you. A moderator will take a look.
circles.reportedHiddenToast: Thank you. The post is hidden while it’s reviewed.
circles.deleteBody: It will be removed for everyone, with any replies.
circles.dangerNote: If someone may be in danger right now, call your local emergency number. Circles can’t send help.
circles.leaveDeletePosts: Also delete everything I posted here
circles.leaveDeleteHint: Replies to your posts are deleted with them.

health.title: Health
health.lead: Look after the basics — sleep, movement and water — keep your own reminders, and know where to get care.
health.notMedical: Waypoint doesn’t diagnose or give medical advice. If you’re worried about your health, talk to a health worker.
health.emergencyNoNumber: In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
health.todayLead: A quick log for you. Only you can see it.
health.activityHint: Walking, cycling, housework, sport — anything that gets you moving.
health.noteHint: How your body feels, symptoms to mention to a doctor, anything. Encrypted.
health.weekLead: No streaks and no scores. Just a picture of the last seven days.
health.weekEmpty: Log a day to see your week here.
health.sleepAverage: Average {hours, number} hours a night, over {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
health.sleepGuide: Most adults need 7 or more hours of sleep a night.
health.activityTotal: {minutes, number} minutes of movement this week.
health.activityGuide: WHO suggests adults get 150–300 minutes of moderate activity a week. Any amount is better than none.
health.waterGuide: Drink water regularly through the day, and more when it’s hot.
health.remindersLead: Medicine, refills, check-ups — anything you want to remember. The words are encrypted; only you can see them.
health.reminderPast: Choose a date and time that hasn’t passed yet.
health.reminderLimit: You have 30 reminders. Delete one before adding another.
health.deleteReminderBody: This reminder will be removed. This can’t be undone.
health.reminderWhere: When a reminder is due, it appears on Today.
health.careLead: Know where to go before you need it.
health.emergencyTitleNoNumber: Call your local emergency number now if someone has:
health.noDrive: Don’t drive yourself. Stay on the line: they’ll tell you what to do.

stroke.title: Signs of a stroke (FAST)
stroke.face: Face: one side droops, or they can’t smile
stroke.arms: Arms: they can’t lift both arms and keep them there
stroke.time: Time: call straight away, even if the signs pass

heart.title: Signs of a heart attack
heart.chest: Crushing or squeezing chest pain, which may spread to the arm, neck or jaw
heart.other: Sweating, feeling sick, or pale, blue or grey skin

allergy.title: A severe allergic reaction
allergy.swelling: Swelling of the throat or tongue
allergy.breathing: Difficulty breathing, wheezing or noisy breathing
allergy.faint: Feeling faint or confused, or cold skin
allergy.action: Use their adrenaline auto-injector if they have one, then call.

heatstroke.title: Heatstroke
heatstroke.signs: Very high temperature, hot skin without sweating, fast breathing
heatstroke.confusion: Confusion, a fit, or passing out
heatstroke.action: Move them somewhere cool, cool their skin with water, and call.

health.notEmergencyNone: A pharmacist or your local clinic can help you decide where to go, often the same day.
health.mindBody: That’s health too. You can talk to someone today.

surroundings.title: Surroundings
surroundings.lead: Weather, air and sun where you are, and what they mean for your day.
surroundings.privacy: Your place stays on this device. Waypoint’s servers never see it.
surroundings.whereLead: Search for a town, or use your location. Either way it stays on this device.
surroundings.locationDenied: Location is turned off for this site. Search for your town instead.
surroundings.locationFailed: We couldn’t get your location. Search for your town instead.
surroundings.noResults: No places found. Check the spelling, or try a bigger town nearby.
surroundings.searchFailed: Search isn’t working right now. Check your connection and try again.
surroundings.failed: Couldn’t load the weather just now.
surroundings.calm: Nothing to watch out for in the next 24 hours.

heat.title: Hot today
heat.body: Avoid hard work or exercise in the hottest hours. Drink water regularly, and check on older neighbours and anyone unwell.

heat-danger.title: Dangerous heat
heat-danger.body: Heatstroke is possible. Stay out of the sun in the middle of the day, keep cool, drink water often and check on people at risk. Heatstroke is an emergency.

cold.title: Freezing temperatures
cold.body: Wear layers, a hat and gloves outside, and keep at least one room warm. Check on older neighbours.

cold-danger.title: Dangerous cold
cold-danger.body: Exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes. Cover up completely, keep time outside short, and watch for shivering, confusion or numb skin.

storm.title: Thunderstorms
storm.body: When you hear thunder, go indoors. Stay away from open ground, water and tall trees.

rain.title: Heavy rain
rain.body: Allow extra time to travel, and never walk or drive through flood water.

wind.title: Strong winds
wind.body: Take care outdoors and near trees, and secure loose things around your home.

uv.title: Strong sun
uv.body: Protect your skin around midday: shade, a shirt, sunscreen and a hat.

uv-extra.title: Very strong sun
uv-extra.body: Avoid being outside around midday. Shade, a shirt, sunscreen and a hat are a must.

air.title: Air unhealthy for some people
air.body: Children, older people and anyone with heart or lung conditions should cut down on long or hard activity outside.

air-danger.title: Unhealthy air
air-danger.body: Everyone should cut down on long or hard activity outside. People with heart or lung conditions should stay indoors if they can.

surroundings.aqiScale: US EPA scale, 0–500. Lower is better.
surroundings.airNone: No air quality data for this place.
surroundings.attribution: Weather and air data by Open-Meteo.com

org.title: Organisations
org.lead: Run programmes for your people — employees, students, residents or members — and see how they’re getting on, without ever seeing anyone individually.
org.guestTitle: Organisation tools need a free account
org.guestBody: Organisations are run from a full account, so colleagues can invite you and nothing is lost. Everything you did as a guest comes with you.
org.mineEmpty: You’re not part of an organisation yet. Set one up below, or ask a colleague to invite you.
org.programmeCount: {count, plural, =0 {No programmes yet} one {# programme} other {# programmes}}

roleHints.owner: Everything, including roles and deleting the organisation

org.createLead: It takes a minute. You’ll be its owner and can invite colleagues afterwards.
org.name: Organisation name
org.limitReached: You already run {limit, number} organisations, the most one person can. Ask a colleague to set up the next one.
org.promiseTitle: What you’ll see — and what you never will
org.promiseSee1: How many people joined each programme, once at least {k, number} of them have agreed to be counted.
org.promiseSee2: Shares such as how many have a plan or moved forward this month, rounded to 5%.
org.promiseSee3: The roles people are aiming for and the skills they’re building, for groups of {k, number} or more.
org.promiseNever1: Names, emails, or any way to tell who joined.
org.promiseNever2: Anything from Mind, Health, Money, Circles, Ask or Shield.
org.promiseNever3: Numbers for small groups, or anything that could single someone out.
org.programmesLead: Each programme has its own join code and link. People join in a minute, on any phone, in their own language.
org.programmesEmpty: Start one for a group you support — a reskilling cohort, a year group, a newcomers’ programme.
org.teamLead: People who can see this organisation’s programmes and totals.
org.inviteLead: They’ll get an email with a link. You can also copy the link and send it yourself.
org.alreadyMember: That person is already in the team.
org.removeBody: They’ll lose access to this organisation’s programmes and totals straight away.
org.leaveBody: You’ll lose access straight away. Someone in the team can invite you back.
org.lastOwner: An organisation needs at least one owner. Make someone else an owner first.
org.thresholdLead: Totals only appear for groups at least this big. Waypoint never goes below {min, number}; you can choose a higher number.
org.deleteBody: Deletes its programmes, join codes, team and settings. People who joined keep everything they did in Waypoint — only their link to your programmes goes.
org.deleteConfirmWord: Type the organisation’s name to confirm
org.programmeNameHint: People see this when they join, for example “Data skills for warehouse teams”.
org.programmeDescriptionHint: A sentence or two: who it’s for, how much time it takes, what support you give.
org.targetRolesHint: Up to 5. People who join see them as suggested paths in Path.
org.datesError: The end date must be after the start.
org.programmeCreated: Programme started. Share its code or link to invite people.
org.inviteProgrammeLead: Share the link, read out the code or put up a poster. Joining is free and takes a minute.
org.messageCopied: Message copied — paste it into an email, chat or newsletter
org.inviteMessage: Join “{programme}” on Waypoint, with {organisation}. It’s free, works on any phone and in your language. Go to {link} or enter the code {code}. {organisation} only ever sees totals for groups of {k, number} or more people — never you.
org.newCodeBody: The current code and link stop working at once, including on printed posters. People who already joined stay in.
org.qrLabel: QR code for the join link
org.insightsLead: Only people who chose to be counted in this programme are included.
org.insightsFew: Totals appear once at least {k, number} people have joined and agreed to be counted. Until then there is nothing to show — which is how it should be.
org.statMoved: finished a step in the last 30 days
org.statOnTarget: are working towards this programme’s roles
org.statHiddenNote: too few people on one side to show safely
org.groupsHidden: Smaller groups are hidden to protect privacy.
org.groupsNone: No group is large enough to show yet.
org.noiseNote: Numbers are rounded and carry a little statistical noise, so nobody can be singled out.
org.closedNotice: This programme is closed: its code no longer lets new people join. Totals stay available.
org.closeBody: Nobody new can join with its code or link. People already in stay in, and totals stay available. You can reopen it later.
org.deleteProgrammeBody: Its code stops working and its totals are gone. People who joined keep everything they did in Waypoint.

invitation.title: Join the team at {organisation}
invitation.body: {inviter} invited you to help run {organisation} on Waypoint.
invitation.signInBody: This invitation was sent to {email}. Sign in, or create an account with that address, to accept it.
invitation.wrongAccount: This invitation was sent to {email}, but you’re signed in with a different address. Sign out, then sign in with {email} to accept it.
invitation.expired: This invitation has expired. Ask {inviter} to send a new one.
invitation.answered: This invitation has already been answered.
invitation.verifyTitle: Confirm your email address to answer
invitation.verifyBody: This invitation was sent to {email}. Links like this can be passed on, so only the confirmed owner of the address can answer. We’ll email you a link: open it, then come back here.

org.insightsAsOf: Figures from {date}; they update once a week, next on {next}.
org.insightsCountAfter: People count from {days, number} days after they choose to be counted.
org.onTargetPending: Target roles changed — back next week
org.thresholdRaiseOnly: You can raise it at any time, but never lower it again: stepping it down and back up would reveal exact numbers.
org.thresholdRaiseBody: Totals will only appear for groups of {k, number} or more people, instead of {from, number}. You won’t be able to lower it again.
org.verifyToInvite: Confirm your email address to invite people — invitations go out in your name.

join.title: Join a programme
join.lead: Employers, colleges, charities and public services run programmes on Waypoint. Enter the code they gave you.
join.codeHint: 8 letters and numbers, for example K7QM-3WXA
join.invalid: That doesn’t look like a join code. Check it and try again.
join.notFound: We couldn’t find a programme with that code. Check it, or ask the organisation for a new one.
join.privacySee: {organisation} only ever sees weekly totals for groups of {k, number} or more people who chose to be counted — for example, how many have a plan.
join.privacyNever: They never see your name, what you write, or anything from Mind, Health, Money, Circles, Ask or Shield.
join.privacyLeave: You can leave at any time in Privacy settings.
join.countMe: Count me in the anonymous totals {organisation} can see
join.countMeHint: Optional, and only for this programme. You can change it any time in Privacy settings.
join.joinedBody: “{programme}” is now part of your Waypoint. Its roles appear as suggestions in Path.
join.countedYes: You’re counted in its anonymous weekly totals, from a week after you chose to be.
join.countedNo: You’re not counted in its totals.
join.closedBody: It isn’t taking new people. If you think that’s a mistake, contact {organisation}.
join.closedNow: This programme has just closed and isn’t taking new people.
join.posterHint: Put it up where people will see it. Choose the poster’s language here — your own settings don’t change.
join.posterOr: Or go to <site></site> and enter this code:
join.posterFree: Free · works on any phone · in your language
join.posterPrivacy: {organisation} only ever sees totals for groups of {k, number} or more people — never you, and never what you write.
join.countMeHintGuest: Optional, and only for this programme. Without an account you are not counted yet: your choice is kept and starts to count once you create an account and confirm your email address. You can change it any time in Privacy settings.
join.countedGuest: You chose to be counted in its anonymous weekly totals. That starts once you create an account and confirm your email address.

admin.title: Admin
admin.lead: Keep Waypoint safe and running. Every action here is recorded.
admin.newThisWeek: {accounts} new accounts and {guests} new guests this week
admin.heldForSafety: posts held for the writer’s safety (never shown)
admin.aiNone: No AI provider is set up — Waypoint is answering in guided mode.
admin.aiCalls: {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}} in the last 30 days
admin.contentLead: Lifelines — emergency numbers, crisis and health lines, where to report scams — are rechecked every 180 days; everything else every year.
admin.allFresh: Every lifeline was checked within the last 180 days.
admin.moderationLead: Posts held as possible scams, hidden after reports, or reported by members. Posts held for the writer’s safety are never shown here.
admin.keepLabel: Keep this post and make it visible
admin.kept: Post kept. The writer has been told if it was hidden.
admin.removed: Post removed. The writer has been told.
admin.removeBody: It’s deleted with any replies, and the writer gets a short note saying it broke the circle guidelines.
admin.safetyCount: {count, plural, =0 {No posts are held for the writer’s safety.} one {# post is held for its writer’s safety. The writer was offered support; the post is never shown to moderators.} other {# posts are held for their writers’ safety. Each writer was offered support; these posts are never shown to moderators.}}
admin.reportsLead: Publish reports that look genuine so people in that country are warned in Shield. Only the category and websites are shown publicly — never the description.
admin.publishedToast: Published — people there will see it in Shield
admin.related: {count, plural, one {# similar report} other {# similar reports}}
admin.auditLead: Who did what: staff and organisation actions. What people do for themselves is never logged here.

actions.org_owner_handed_over: Handed an organisation to a new owner
actions.forecast_verdict_confirmed: Forecast outcome confirmed by a second person

admin.worriedNote: A member was worried about the writer, not the post. Waypoint has already sent the writer a private note about where to find support; keeping the post is usually right.
admin.contentGeneral: {count, plural, one {# is general guidance} other {# are general guidance}}
admin.channelsLead: The last 30 days. Only counts are kept: never numbers, and never what anyone wrote.
admin.channelsNone: No text channel is set up yet
admin.channelsNoneBody: Until an SMS, WhatsApp or USSD provider is added, people can only use Waypoint on the web. The setup guide is docs/CHANNELS.md.
admin.channelOutNote: Sent: {ai, plural, one {# AI answer} other {# AI answers}} and {codes, plural, one {# sign-in code} other {# sign-in codes}}.
admin.forecastsLead: Publish a question with a chance and its sources, then judge it on its date. Every forecast that is judged goes on the public record.
admin.forecastFixed: Once published, the question, how it is judged and the date can’t be changed. If one of them is wrong, withdraw the forecast and publish it again.
admin.fQuestionHint: A yes-or-no question about something that can be checked on a date. End it with a question mark.
admin.fWhatToDo: What people can do about it
admin.fWhatToDoHint: Useful whichever way it turns out.
admin.fCriteriaHint: Exactly what counts as yes, and the source you will check.
admin.fRegionsHint: Two-letter codes separated by commas, for example KE, TZ. Leave empty for everywhere.
admin.fProbabilityHint: From 1 to 99. Nothing about the future is certain.
admin.fBaseRate: How often this usually happens, in percent
admin.fSourcesHint: One on each line: the name, a comma, then the full https:// address. At least one.
admin.fCheck: Some fields need attention. Check the question mark, the chance (1 to 99), the sources and the date.
admin.tHint: Write translations yourself: forecasts are never machine-translated. Without one, people see the original with its language named.
admin.aNote: What happened, or why it can’t be judged
admin.aOnce: This is recorded once and can’t be undone: it becomes part of the public record.
admin.cLead: An outcome stands as soon as it is recorded, and is marked “not yet double-checked” in public until a different member of staff confirms it here.
admin.cYours: Awaiting a second check. You recorded this outcome, so someone else has to confirm it.
admin.cConfirmBody: Confirm only if you have checked the source yourself and agree with what was recorded. This is logged under your name and can’t be undone.
admin.eCheck: Some fields need attention. Check the advice, the sources (name, comma, https:// address) and any translation you started.
admin.eClosed: This forecast can no longer be changed: its date has passed or it has been judged.
admin.tFixed: This translation’s question and how it is judged are fixed now that it is saved. Its explanation and advice can still change.
admin.tFixedOnSave: Once saved, a translation’s question and how it is judged can’t be changed.
admin.signalsLead: Things that changed, each with the source staff read it in. A signal is shown straight away to the people it is about.
admin.signalsEmpty: No signals have been added yet.
admin.sSourceNeeded: A signal is never published without a source people can open. Waypoint doesn’t write signals: add only what you have read yourself at the address you give.
admin.sTitleHint: One plain sentence, like a headline.
admin.sSummaryHint: In your own words: what changed, for whom, and from when. Don’t copy the source.
admin.sSectorsHint: Short English words separated by commas, for example agriculture, transport.
admin.sCheck: Some fields need attention. Check the summary, the source name and address (https://) and the date.
admin.sNotShown: No longer shown to anyone: it is more than a year old.
admin.sWithdrawBody: It will no longer be shown to anyone, including people who saved it. The activity log keeps its title and source.
admin.feedbackLead: What people told us worked or didn’t, newest first. Personal details were removed from each message before it was kept. Nobody is named unless they asked for a reply, and a guest can’t be identified at all.

byText.title: Waypoint by text
byText.metaDescription: Reach Waypoint by SMS, WhatsApp or USSD: help lines, scam checks and answers, with no smartphone or data needed.
byText.lead: No smartphone, or no data? You can still reach Waypoint by text: help lines for your country, scam checks, and answers to your questions.
byText.cost: Waypoint is free. Your mobile network may charge its usual rate for texts.

sms.title: SMS
sms.body: Text HELLO to this number to start.

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp
whatsapp.body: Send us a message on WhatsApp.

ussd.title: USSD
ussd.body: Dial this code for a simple menu. It works on any phone.

byText.noneBody: You can use everything on this website, and help lines for your country are always on the support page.
byText.tryLead: A real reply to a message someone wasn’t sure about.
byText.sampleCheck: CHECK Your parcel is on hold. Pay the 1.99 delivery fee today or it will be returned: parcel-help.info/pay
byText.commandsLead: Capital letters aren’t needed, and the words work in all our languages.

help.what: Help lines for your country, with the emergency number first.

check.what: Checks a message for signs of a scam. You can also just forward it to us.

ask.what: A short answer. For a job plan or a money check, the website can do more.

lang.what: Change language: LANG 3 for Español, LANG 7 for Kiswahili.

country.what: Your country, in two letters, for local numbers.

ai.what: Turn fuller answers from our AI assistant on or off.

stop.what: No more texts from us. START brings you back.

byText.privacyBody: Never what you write. We keep your number sealed (encrypted), with your language, your country and the choices you make. If you don’t text us for 180 days, we forget your number.
byText.aiTitle: AI only if you say yes
byText.aiBody: Safety replies, help lines and scam checks never use AI. Your questions go to our AI assistant only after you text AI YES, with numbers and email addresses removed first (names aren’t, so leave them out), and its answers start with “AI:”.
byText.dangerBody: Call your local emergency number. If you text us about something serious, we reply with help lines first, and you can text HELP at any time.

legal.operator: This Waypoint is run by {operator}. In these pages, “we” means them.
legal.operatorMissing: The people who run this Waypoint haven’t added their name and contact details here yet. You can still see, download and delete your information yourself, in Settings.
legal.dataLocation: Its servers and database are in {place}.
legal.contact: Write to <link>{email}</link> about your information or these terms.
legal.contactMissing: There’s no contact address here yet. You can still see, download and delete your information yourself, in Settings.
legal.notInUse: Not set up on this Waypoint.
legal.appNote: In the phone app, Settings are under More.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: What Waypoint collects, why, how long it keeps it and the choices you have — in plain words.

short.optional: Nothing optional is on until you turn it on, and you can turn it off again at any time.
short.encrypted: Private things — your journal, mood and health notes, goals, money details and trusted contacts — are encrypted, each person’s with their own key.
short.never: We never sell your information, show you ads or track you across the web.
short.organisations: Organisations only ever see rounded totals for groups of at least {k} people — and only if you choose to be counted.
short.control: You can download everything, or delete your account, yourself at any time.

collect.title: What we collect, and why
collect.lead: Only what Waypoint needs to help you. Help lines and scam checks work without an account.
collect.account: Your email address and a password or passkey — or nothing, if you stay a guest
collect.accountWhy: To sign you in, once you’ve confirmed your address with the link we email you. Passwords are kept only in a scrambled form (a hash) that can’t be turned back into the password.
collect.profile: Your country, language and time zone, the name you’d like us to use, and what’s going on for you
collect.profileWhy: To show the right next steps, plans, services and emergency numbers.
collect.writing: What you write: conversations in Ask, plans, goals, check-ins, journal entries and posts in circles
collect.writingWhy: To keep them for you and help you with them.
collect.phone: Your phone number, if you add it (proved with a code) or text Waypoint
collect.phoneWhy: To answer you by text or WhatsApp, and to send sign-in codes.
collect.security: A cookie that keeps you signed in, and scrambled versions of network (IP) addresses
collect.securityWhy: To keep your account safe and stop abuse. We never keep the addresses themselves.

never.title: What we never keep
never.scam: Messages you check with Scam Shield. We keep only a fingerprint of the text, the result, which warning signs matched and the names of any websites it links to — enough to spot scams going round.
never.crisis: The words that made Waypoint show crisis support. We keep only that it happened, how serious it looked and which rule matched.
never.location: Where you are. Weather and air quality come to your browser straight from the forecast service, for a place rounded to about 1 km, and the place you choose stays on your device.
never.tracking: Advertising cookies, tracking cookies or analytics that follow you. Our only cookies keep you signed in, remember that this device has signed in before (so someone guessing your password can’t lock you out), and remember your language, time zone and display choices, and which steps you set aside for today.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.lead: Each of these is off until you turn it on. Change them at any time in Settings → Privacy & data.

ai.title: AI and Ask
ai.guide: Waypoint’s guide is an AI, not a person. Before any AI sees a message, Waypoint checks it for signs of crisis — and if you might be in danger, it shows emergency and support numbers first.
ai.off: Unless you turn on “Use AI providers”, nothing you write in Ask goes to an outside AI: Ask answers with guided replies, or with a model on Waypoint’s own servers if one is set up.
ai.on: If you turn it on, an AI provider gets a copy of your conversation to write each reply — with your goals, what you asked it to remember and your current plan, when you have allowed those to be used — and your goal and country when it writes you a plan. Email addresses, phone numbers and card, bank and ID numbers are removed first. Names aren’t removed, so leave them out.
ai.shield: Scam Shield asks an AI for a second opinion only with that choice on, or when you ask for one on a single message — and the copy it sends is cleaned the same way.
ai.noProviders: This Waypoint has no outside AI provider set up, so nothing is sent to one.
ai.training: We don’t use what you write to train AI.
ai.approval: When the guide wants to save something for you — a plan step, a reminder, a note — it asks first. Nothing is saved until you press Allow.

crisis.title: If you may be in danger
crisis.body: If something you write suggests you may be in danger, Waypoint shows emergency and support numbers for your country straight away, and may check in with you later on Today.
crisis.contact: Waypoint never contacts anyone for you. If you add a trusted contact, a message goes to them only when you choose to send it.

share.title: Who else handles your information
share.lead: Only the services Waypoint needs, each with only what it needs. We never sell anything.
share.aiGets: A copy of your conversation with personal numbers removed — only if you turned on “Use AI providers”, or asked Scam Shield for a second opinion.
share.textingGets: Your number and the messages, when you text Waypoint or ask for a sign-in code.
share.emailGets: Your email address and the message, for sign-in links, confirmations and invitations.
share.weatherGets: A rounded location, asked for by your own browser — it never passes through Waypoint.
share.hosting: The company that runs Waypoint’s servers
share.hostingGets: Everything Waypoint stores, encrypted where this notice says so.
share.organisationsGets: Rounded totals for groups of at least {k} people — only if you choose to be counted for that programme. Never your name or anything you write.
share.authoritiesGets: Only what the law makes us give. Where the law allows, we’ll tell you.

keep.title: How long we keep things
keep.conversationsTime: As long as you choose: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days (the starting setting), a year, or until you delete them.
keep.guestsTime: Deleted after 180 days without use, with everything in them.
keep.unconfirmed: Accounts whose email address is never confirmed

security.title: How we protect it
security.encryption: Private notes, health and money details, goals and trusted contacts are encrypted in the database with a key made for you. Deleting your account destroys that key first, so they can never be read again.
security.sessions: You’re signed out after 30 days without using Waypoint, and sessions don’t record where you connect from.
security.staff: Staff tools show only what staff need — posts held for review, scam reports and overall counts — never your conversations, notes, health or money details. What staff do is recorded.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.lead: Wherever you live, you can do all of this yourself, straight away:
rights.see: See and download everything we hold about you: Settings → Privacy & data → Download my data.
rights.correct: Correct it: change your details in Settings at any time.
rights.delete: Delete it: Settings → Privacy & data → Delete my account. It’s immediate and can’t be undone.
rights.withdraw: Change your mind: switch any choice off, and it stops from then on.
rights.complain: Complain: write to us, or to the data protection authority where you live.
rights.memory: See what Waypoint was asked to remember, and delete any of it: Settings → Privacy & data → What Waypoint remembers. Switching memory off stops it being used or added to; what is there stays until you delete it.

children.title: Children and young people
children.body: You need to be at least {age} to use Waypoint’s personal features — or older, if the law where you live sets a higher age for agreeing to this. Help lines and scam checks are open to everyone, with no account.
children.remove: If you think a child under that age has given us information, write to us and we’ll delete it.

transfers.title: Where your information is
transfers.body: Some of the services above may be in other countries. Where the law requires it, we put agreements in place so your information stays protected there too.

changes.title: Changes to this notice
changes.body: When we change this notice in a way that matters, we’ll say so here and in Waypoint before the change applies. We will never use your information in a new way you haven’t agreed to.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: The agreement between you and the people who run this Waypoint, in plain words.

short.guidance: Waypoint gives guidance, not professional advice. Check anything important with someone qualified.
short.emergency: In danger? Call your local emergency number. Waypoint can’t call anyone for you.
short.kind: Be kind, and keep other people’s information to yourself.
short.yours: What you write is yours, and you can delete it at any time.

about.title: About these terms
about.body: These terms apply whenever you use Waypoint — on the web, in the app or by text message. By using Waypoint, you agree to them; if you don’t agree, please don’t use it. The privacy notice explains what happens to your information.

what.title: What Waypoint is — and isn’t
what.body: Waypoint is a free guide for big changes in life. It gives information and suggestions to help you decide what to do next.
what.advice: It isn’t medical, mental health, legal, financial or immigration advice, and it doesn’t replace a doctor, counsellor, lawyer or adviser.
what.ai: Its guide is an AI. It can be wrong, out of date or miss something, so check anything important before you act on it.
what.shield: Scam Shield gives a warning, not a guarantee. A message can be a scam even when Shield doesn’t flag it — never send money or codes to someone you can’t check.
what.forecasts: Forecasts about jobs, prices and the world are estimates, not promises.
what.services: Help lines, courses and services we list are run by others. We check them, but we aren’t responsible for what they do.

emergency.title: Not an emergency service
emergency.body: If you or someone else is in danger, call your local emergency number now. Waypoint shows the numbers, but it can’t call anyone for you, and nobody watches conversations as they happen.

who.title: Who can use Waypoint
who.age: You need to be at least {age} — or older, if the law where you live sets a higher age for using services like this.
who.account: Keep your password or passkey to yourself, and tell us if you think someone else has used your account.
who.guest: As a guest, your information is linked to this browser or phone. If you sign out or clear it, you can’t get back in — create an account to keep it: it moves into the account the first time you sign in to it on the same device. If someone signs in to a different account there, what was done as a guest is deleted unless they choose to bring it along.

fair.title: Using Waypoint fairly
fair.harm: Don’t harass, threaten or bully anyone, or encourage anyone to hurt themselves or others.
fair.private: Don’t share other people’s private information, and don’t pretend to be someone you’re not.
fair.illegal: Don’t use Waypoint to scam, spam or do anything illegal.
fair.break: Don’t try to break in, overload Waypoint, copy it in bulk, or get round its limits or safety checks.
fair.identify: Don’t try to work out who someone is from an organisation’s totals or anything else Waypoint shows.

circles.title: Circles
circles.body: Circles are small groups where people going through similar things support each other. Be kind, keep what members share inside the circle, and use a name you’re comfortable with.
circles.moderation: Posts that look like a crisis or a scam are held back, and posts that members report may be hidden until someone reviews them. We may remove posts that break these terms.

content.title: What you write
content.body: What you write is yours. You let us store and use it only to run Waypoint for you — for example, to keep your plans, or to show your circle posts to that circle’s members. We don’t sell it, and we don’t use it to train AI.
content.reports: Scam reports you send may be used, without your name, to warn other people.

organisations.title: For organisations
organisations.body: If you run a programme on Waypoint for an organisation, you also agree not to pressure anyone to join it or to be counted, not to try to identify anyone from its totals, and to give access only to staff who need it.

texting.title: Texting Waypoint
texting.body: Waypoint doesn’t charge for texts, but your mobile operator may charge its usual rates. Text STOP at any time to stop messages.

service.title: The service
service.body: Waypoint is free for individuals. We work to keep it running and accurate, but we can’t promise it will always be available or free of mistakes.
service.changes: We may add, change or remove features. If a change affects you in an important way, we’ll tell you first.

ending.title: Ending
ending.you: You can stop using Waypoint and delete your account at any time, in Settings → Privacy & data.
ending.us: We may suspend or close an account that seriously or repeatedly breaks these terms, or that puts other people at risk.

liability.title: Responsibility
liability.body: Waypoint is provided as it is. As far as the law allows, we aren’t responsible for decisions you make based on it, or for what services run by others do.
liability.rights: Nothing in these terms takes away rights you have by law where you live.

law.title: Which law applies
law.body: These terms follow the law of the country where the people who run this Waypoint are based. If you live somewhere else, you keep the protection of your own country’s consumer law, and you can go to court there.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: If we change these terms in a way that matters, we’ll say so here and in Waypoint before the change applies. If you keep using Waypoint after that, the new terms apply.

welcome.offlineBody: Help lines and scam checks work even with no connection. What you check stays on your phone.
welcome.startHint: No account needed. You can add one later.

shield.private: The check runs on your phone. Nothing is sent unless you ask for a second opinion.
shield.checkedOnPhone: Checked on your phone. Nothing was sent.
shield.checkedOnline: Checked by Waypoint online. The message wasn’t stored.
shield.secondOpinionHint: Sends the message to Waypoint to check again (it isn’t stored) and, where available, a redacted copy to our AI provider.
shield.offlineSecondOpinion: You’re offline. The check on your phone still works; ask for a second opinion when you’re connected.

ask.offline: You’re offline. Ask needs a connection — help lines and scam checks still work.
ask.aiOn: AI answers are on. You can turn them off in More, under Privacy & data.
ask.aiOnNext: AI answers are on from your next message.

help.fromPhone: Based on your phone’s region. Choose another country if that’s not where you are.
help.noCountry: Choose your country to see local help lines.

country.lead: Help lines, scam reporting and local advice follow this country.
country.noMatch: No country with that name. We add countries once their help lines are checked.

language.note: Translations are still being reviewed. Tell us if something reads wrong.
language.restartBody: This language reads in the other direction. Waypoint needs to restart to turn the layout around.

more.noAccount: You’re using Waypoint without an account. Help lines and scam checks never need one.
more.privacyHint: What Waypoint may do with your information
more.websiteLead: Plans, money, goals, groups and more open in your browser. Sign in there with your account to see the same things.

account.created: Check your email: open the link we sent to confirm your address, then sign in with your password.

forecasts.title: What’s next?
forecasts.lead: Things that may happen, how likely we think they are, and what you can do either way.
forecasts.honest: Nobody can know the future. These are estimates, each with its sources, and we publish how every one turns out.
forecasts.empty: No forecasts have been published yet.
forecasts.awaitingLead: The date has passed. We’ll say how each one turned out as soon as it can be checked.
forecasts.recordLead: Every forecast we publish is judged on its date, and the result stays here, right or wrong.
forecasts.scoreExplain: 0 is perfect. Saying “50%” every time scores 0.25. Lower is better.
forecasts.referenceLine: Always giving the usual rate would have scored {score}.
forecasts.tooFew: Judged so far: {count, number}. A score means little before {min, number}, so we don’t show one yet.
forecasts.calibrationTitle: When we gave a chance, how often did it happen?
forecasts.calibrationLead: If our chances are honest, things we call 70% should happen about 7 times in 10.
forecasts.calibrationTooFew: We’ll show this once {min, number} forecasts have been judged. With fewer, it would say more about luck than about us.
forecasts.how1: Each forecast says in advance exactly what will count as “yes”, and on which day.
forecasts.how2: On that day staff check it against a source anyone can open, and record yes or no.
forecasts.how3: A forecast is scored on the chance it showed each day it was open, so changing the number at the last minute counts for very little.
forecasts.how4: If a question turns out to be impossible to judge, it is withdrawn and listed with the reason. It isn’t scored.
forecasts.recordEmpty: No forecast has been judged yet.
forecasts.itsScore: Score for this forecast: {score}. 0 is perfect; saying 50% scores 0.25.
forecasts.how5: Every chance a forecast showed stays listed with its date, and staff record the outcome as soon as it is known. A number changed after the fact is there for anyone to see.
forecasts.unchecked: Not yet double-checked: a second member of our staff has not confirmed this outcome.
forecasts.how6: A second member of staff checks each outcome. Until they have, the forecast is marked “not yet double-checked”.
forecasts.uncheckedCount: {count, plural, one {# outcome has} other {# outcomes have}} not been double-checked yet.
